definitions.gloss: rice planting; transplanting rice seedlings into a paddy
definitions.explanation: The agricultural work of transplanting young rice plants from a nursery bed into a flooded paddy field, typically done in late spring to early summer.

examples.japanese: {田植|たう}え⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧になった。
{子|こ}どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{田植|たう}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{体験|たいけん}した→体験する：09858_taikensuru⟧。
⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{天候不順|てんこうふじゅん}で{田植|たう}え⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{遅|おく}れている→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: This year, there are regions where rice planting has been delayed due to bad weather.

notes:
Refers specifically to the transplanting of rice seedlings (⟦{苗|なえ}→苗：05489_nae⟧) into a flooded paddy field (⟦{田|た}んぼ→田んぼ：00402_tanbo⟧). Traditionally done by hand, now largely mechanized with rice-planting machines ({田植|たう}え{機|き}). The rice-planting season is typically May to June in most of Japan and is closely tied to seasonal awareness in Japanese culture.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {田植|たう}え{機|き}: rice-planting machine
- {田植|たう}え⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧: rice-planting season
- {田植|たう}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to plant rice
- {手|て}{植|う}え: hand-planting (of rice)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{田植|たう}え has traditionally been accompanied by rituals and festivals. {御田植祭|おたうえまつり} (rice-planting festivals) are still held at many shrines. School field trips to rice paddies for {田植|たう}え⟦{体験|たいけん}→体験：11443_taiken⟧ (rice-planting experience) are common in Japanese elementary education.
